learning_outcomes.text: Knows and understands basic concepts of electric field in high voltage application aspect.
Possesses knowledge about issues of electrical strength of solid, liquid and gaseous dielectrics.
Knows and understands issues of overvoltages and overvoltage protection.
Possesses knowledge about issues of testing and measurement techniques.
Knows basic principles of safe work in the High Voltage Laboratory. Knows the principle of operation of testing devices and safety measures used in the laboratory.
Understands the phenomenon of electrical corona and the phenomenon of capacitive voltage distribution in layered insulation systems.
Knows the effects caused by the presence of electric field in insulation systems.
Knows the principle of operation and construction of devices located in the High Voltage Laboratory.
Can predict the type of discharges occurring in the insulation system based on the geometry of this system.
Can select appropriate research apparatus for the task assigned.
Can perform voltage tests in the presence of the instructor. Can analyze experimental results.
Is aware of the dangers associated with working with high voltage.
Is aware of the rapid development of technical sciences and technologies used in power engineering.

syllabus_topics: High Voltage Laboratories - equipment, organization, safe working principles: Organization of work in a high voltage laboratory. Principles of safe work in the laboratory. Equipment of the High Voltage Laboratory

Basic information on high voltage technology: Dielectrics and their properties. Types and structures of dielectrics. Conductive properties. Dielectric losses. Ionization and deionization processes. Electrical stresses of dielectrics. Field inhomogeneity coefficient and methods of stress evaluation. Dielectric stresses in layered systems. Technical insulation systems. Practical and ideal system. High voltage laboratory systems

Testing of AC, DC and impulse voltage testing systems: Construction and operating principle of the TP110 testing transformer and a cascade of 2xTP110 transformers. Operating principle of the GU400 impulse voltage generator

Electrical strength of materials and insulation systems: Electrical strength of systems with gaseous dielectrics. Development of discharge in gaseous dielectrics. Critical voltage and stress. Corona phenomena and static strength of air. Impulse strength of air systems. Strength of systems with liquid dielectrics. Discharge mechanisms in liquids. Strength of solid dielectrics. Breakdown mechanisms of dielectrics. Strength of composite systems.

Methods of measuring AC, DC and impulse high voltages: Construction and operating principle of high-voltage measuring instruments. Voltage measurement using a sphere gap, electrostatic voltmeter, voltage divider and series capacitor with a rectifier.

Overvoltages: General characteristics of overvoltages. Overvoltage waves in lines and windings. Waves at discontinuity points (nodes). Multiple wave reflections. Power and energy of waves. Lightning hazard and atmospheric overvoltages. Parameters of lightning discharges. Overvoltages in power lines. Internal overvoltages. Dynamic overvoltages. Resonant and ferroresonant overvoltages.

Overvoltage and lightning protection: Surge arresters and lightning protection devices. Spark gaps. Expulsion arresters. Varistor surge arresters. Air terminals and down conductors. Earthing. Insulation coordination. Voltage levels. Principles of lightning and overvoltage protection. Protection of lines and substations. Principles of protection of building structures. Principles of protection of electrical installations against overvoltages. Elimination of disturbances and voltage hazards
Testing of voltage distribution in insulation systems: Testing of voltage distribution in high voltage insulation systems using the example of a layered flat capacitor.

Testing and measurement technique: Testing devices. AC voltage testing set. DC voltage power supplies. Lightning and switching impulse voltage generators. Impulse current generators. Measuring apparatus. Measuring spark gaps. Electrostatic voltmeters. Voltage dividers. Peak value meters.
Testing of electrical corona: Testing of electrical corona phenomenon in a model of a power line. Influence of bundled conductors on reducing the electric field intensity around the phase conductor.

Testing of electrical discharges in air insulation systems: Testing of surface and creeping discharges in high voltage insulation systems. Support type insulation system and bushing type insulation system. Surface and creeping discharges.

Testing of wave phenomena in power systems: Testing of wave phenomena in power line models. Wave reflection phenomenon resulting from discontinuities in a long line. Effects resulting from mismatch of wave impedances.

Testing of temporary overvoltages in power systems: Testing of ferroresonance phenomenon and related overvoltages. Testing of earth fault overvoltages occurring in a network with an isolated neutral point.

Testing of switching overvoltages in power systems: Switching overvoltages occurring as a result of switching operations performed in the network. Operating principle and understanding of circuit breaker properties.
assessment_rules: Lectures are assessed through activity during classes, tests, and an examination. Laboratory classes are assessed through activity during classes, participation in a discussion, tests, an examination, and reports. Students must be prepared for laboratory exercises, which may be verified by an oral or written colloquium. Passing the laboratory classes requires presenting a solution to the posed problem and passing all laboratory sessions. Passing the module is possible after passing all laboratory classes.
